items.method: Cross-read the market-heatmap breadth percentage against its 60% threshold and against the benchmark's distance from its 52-week high and its moving-average stack, then overlay the option-flow call fraction and put-versus-call premium and the VIX band to judge whether an index holding near highs is being carried by a narrowing set of leaders.
items.note: A narrow-leadership divergence persists into this morning window. The SPY benchmark trades at 769.2, only 1.12% under its 52-week high, in a bull-stacked moving-average regime (50-day distance +2.72%, 200-day +9.39%, 126-day momentum +13.43%), yet only 26.1% of the 134 market-heatmap constituents are positive on the day — a 33.9-point shortfall to the 60% broad-participation threshold. Premium flow is not confirming the strength: it reads balanced, with calls just 43.6% of premium (about $435.2M of call premium against $563.8M of puts) across 12 tickers and 737 flagged contracts. VIX 15.79 keeps this in a calm, pressure-not-panic band, and swing structure still reads bull-stacked with an active double bottom. A headline index pinned near its high on 26% breadth while hedging demand modestly leads is the classic thinning-leadership pattern, where the average stock is already lagging beneath a firm index. This is what to watch: whether breadth re-broadens back toward the threshold or the index converges down toward a narrowing tape.
items.title: Index sits about 1% under its 52-week high in a bull-stacked regime while daily breadth holds at 26% and premium flow is balanced-to-defensive

inputs: options-structure-lab.regime=negative; signedNetGEX=-3.54B; flip=773.07; callWall=773; putWall=768; expectedMove=4.2; spot=768.29; atmIV=0.1476

items.method: Read the options-structure signed net-gamma sign with its flip and wall levels against current spot, size the expected-move band, confirm the dealer scenario and hold from the gamma playbook, then overlay the most-unusual option prints and the prior-session intraday VWAP to judge whether short-gamma dealers are positioned to accelerate a break of the nearest wall.
items.note: Dealer positioning and price have converged on the lower edge of the gamma structure this window. Signed net gamma is negative at about -$3.54B, and SPY spot 768.29 has slipped below the 773.07 flip to sit right at the 768 put wall with the 773 call wall overhead. The front expected move is a tight plus or minus 4.2, so the 768-to-773 wall corridor is narrow and the two walls essentially bracket spot. Under negative gamma dealers hedge in the direction of the move, so pressure at a wall tends to extend rather than mean-revert. The flow tape agrees at the exact level: among the most unusual prints is a same-day SPY 768 put at $20.0M on 40.9x open interest, printed straight on the put wall, alongside a same-day QQQ 719 put and a longer-dated AMD 480 put. The prior live auction was a range-day under mixed control with VWAP 768.65 sitting just above spot. This is a coiled range-break-watch structure with a patient, same-session-fade playbook: while 768 holds and VIX 15.79 stays calm it can stay orderly, but a sustained loss of the 768 put wall in short-gamma is the level that would tip the balance toward downside acceleration rather than a fade.
items.title: SPY spot rests on the 768 put wall below the 773.07 negative-gamma flip as the same-day tape sells the put wall directly
